questions.q: What is the one required argument on the aws_vpc resource?
options: availability_zone
name
address_space
cidr_block
questions.explain: aws_vpc's required argument is cidr_block — unlike azurerm_virtual_network, it has no name argument at all.

questions.q: Why does the aws provider block need a region argument when azurerm's provider block only needed features {}?
options: azurerm actually requires a region too, this lesson just omitted it
aws_vpc resources ignore the provider block entirely
region is a deprecated legacy argument with no real effect
AWS has no single global endpoint — every API call the aws provider makes is scoped to one region
questions.explain: Unlike Azure Resource Manager, AWS requires the provider to know which region every API call targets, so region is required on the aws provider block.

questions.q: In aws_subnet.web, what does vpc_id = aws_vpc.example.id reference, and how does that differ from azurerm_subnet's virtual_network_name?
options: A hardcoded AWS account number
The subnet's own CIDR block
A generated identifier AWS assigns at create time, whereas virtual_network_name referenced a plain name string chosen by the author
The literal string "example", with no real difference from azurerm
questions.explain: aws_subnet references its VPC by a generated id (something like vpc-0abc123456789def0), while azurerm_subnet referenced its VNet by the plain name string you chose.

questions.q: What does availability_zone do on an aws_subnet resource?
options: Pins the subnet to exactly one Availability Zone for its entire life
Sets the subnet's CIDR block
Has no effect unless Multi-AZ is separately enabled
Names the VPC the subnet belongs to
questions.explain: A subnet is tied to one AZ permanently — which is why high-availability designs create matching subnets in multiple AZs, as this lesson's web/app subnets do.

questions.q: Since aws_vpc has no name argument, how do you give it a human-readable label that shows up in the AWS console?
options: Set a Name key inside the resource's tags map
It isn't possible — AWS resources never display a name
Rename the Terraform resource's local name
AWS automatically generates a display name from the cidr_block
questions.explain: The AWS console's display name comes from a Name entry inside the generic tags map, a convention shared across nearly every AWS resource type, not a dedicated schema argument.
